The Agent Arena Hackathon
San Francisco, CASep 26 at 9:00 AM – Sep 27 at 5:00 PM (PDT)

Join us at The Agent Arena Hackathon hosted by Vultr to build what the next generation of agent infrastructure actually looks like in production.

Agents are writing code, driving browsers, and running real operations for teams. The infrastructure built to contain and coordinate what they do needs to get better.

Vultr is bringing the tools for you to build infrastructure powering the next generation of autonomous execution: VM backends, serverless inference, and the compute layer agents run on when they stop talking and start acting.

Compete for more than $10,000 across cash and credits!

Note: This event is fully in-person in San Francisco. Teams may have up to four members. All attendees must apply and be approved. Submitting an application does not guarantee a seat; approved applicants must confirm their attendance.

About Event

What if you could see 10 AI tools in action, try them yourself, and use them to solve real problems — all in one session?
Buildfest: Demos and Challenges is a demo day, hands-on event where sponsors will show you what their tools can do, and then give you a small challenge to solve.
No long workshops. No hours of setup.
You’ll see → try → build → solve.
Whether you're a developer, student, founder, designer, researcher, or just curious about AI, you can jump in at your level.
Event Format
You’ll start with a set of 10 sample datasets covering different real-world problems. You can choose one of them to work with, or bring your own dataset and problem.

sample_datasets.pdf
546.9 KB

PS: You can convert the pdf to excel through online convertor
Pick a problem
You can work on problems like: Build a system that creates study plans for students, Help shoppers find the right product based on their needs, Automate information extraction and processing from invoices, Build an AI travel planner, Summarize notes and extract important actions, Match candidates to jobs and help recruiters screen applications, Analyze restaurant data and identify inventory/demand problems, Build an AI system that answers common customer questions, Turn a simple idea into a structured content workflow, Find and evaluate promising problems and ideas or choose your own problem and build something that matters to you.
How It Works
Each sponsor will have a short demo + challenge.
First, they'll show you their product in action and explain what it does, why it is useful, and how you can use it.
Then you'll get a small challenge where you can try the tool yourself.
You don't need to use every tool. Use whichever sponsor tools make sense for your problem — one, several, or all of them.
The goal is to understand how each tool can be used and then combine the right tools to solve a problem.

Welcome, event overview, and introduction to the demo session.
4:35–4:40 PM — BuilderBase @ Sean Chiu
Create better events with BuilderBase.

Figure out what to build with AI, what to automate, and where humans add the most value.
5:25–5:35 PM — Rocket Ride @ Joe Maionchi
Build AI and data pipelines directly in your IDE, from raw data to structured output.

Discover and recommend products using context like fit, color, material, reviews, and images.

Package and run code anywhere with WebAssembly.

Turn team conversations and questions into actionable results with AI.
6:05–6:15 PM — Unlimit @ Robin Meister
Move money across borders by connecting global payments, financial accounts, and digital asset rails.
6:15–6:25 PM — Lore @ Kaia Colban
Bring people and AI agents together to collaborate on work-in-progress and learn from each other.

Give AI agents reliable, real-time access to the web across 195+ countries.
6:35–6:45 PM — Light Sage @ Sean Er
Help AI agents discover, evaluate, and use your APIs, CLIs, and MCPs more effectively.
6:45–6:50 PM — Bridge US @ Vin Wanfan
Match the right people with each other at events.
You Can Mix and Match Tools
The challenges are not isolated.
You can use one tool, several tools, or all of the sponsor tools to solve your problem.
For example, you could:
Choose a problem → use Ask the W to plan it → use Flatkey to choose a model → build a pipeline with Rocket Ride → create multiple agents with Kylon → do code review in Tenki → Run workload in wasmer.
Or ignore that entire workflow and create your own.
The point is to experiment and discover how different AI tools fit together.
Sponsors
Tenki
Tenki provides sandbox environments, cloud compute, and runners for executing code and workloads. It gives builders a place to experiment, run, and scale their work.
Rocket Ride
Rocket Ride helps developers build AI and data pipelines directly in their IDE. It makes it easier to connect data, AI models, processing steps, and outputs into repeatable workflows.
Flatkey
Flatkey is a unified access layer for AI, connecting teams to 328+ official AI models through one API. It supports models from providers such as GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and more, with transparent pricing and automatic failover.
FinChip
FinChip provides agent skills that give AI agents reusable capabilities for performing specific tasks. Skills can help make agents more useful, structured, and consistent.
Kylon
Kylon helps you create AI agents that can run business processes. You can turn workflows into agents that understand tasks, use tools, and take actions.
Ask the W
Ask the W helps you figure out what is worth building with AI. It helps identify good ideas, tasks that can be handled by agents, places where human judgment is needed, and the next steps to take.
Sartorial
Sartorial helps make products more intelligently discoverable and recommendable. It adds context such as social proof, material, fit, color, promotions, image meaning, and brand-specific ranking judgment to product discovery.
Wasmer
Wasmer provides a way to execute WebAssembly universally. It helps developers package and run code across different environments in a portable and consistent way.
PromptQL
PromptQL is a multiplayer AI workspace with a built-in Wiki for AI-first teams. Think of it like Slack for teams working with AI — where conversations can turn into shared knowledge, decisions, and execution.
Unlimit
Unlimit is the global financial infrastructure for the borderless agentic economy. Designed to bridge the gap between fragmented local markets and the future of autonomous commerce, Unlimit provides the programmable operating layer for the world’s most ambitious businesses.
Light Sage
Light Sage builds infrastructure for the agent economy, helping companies track and improve how AI agents discover and use their APIs, CLIs, and MCPs. It also created DevToolArena, a benchmark for developer tools.
Massive
Massive provides web access for AI agents, models, and data pipelines through millions of volunteer devices across 195+ countries. Its API enables reliable, real-time access to websites at scale.
Lore
Lore enables teams and their AI agents to collaborate on work-in-progress across tools like Claude, Codex, and Cowork. It brings knowledge work out of silos so people and agents can learn from each other as they work.
AdaL
AdaL is an automation-first agent harness designed to get more done with less of your time. She combines personality, skills, and memory to become a personalized agent that can work alongside you.

About Event
​TrueFoundry Agent Harness Hackathon

​AI agents are easy to prototype and much harder to run in production. Once an agent touches real users, tools, data, budgets, and internal systems, the work becomes less about a clever prompt and more about routing, permissions, tracing, retries, evals, guardrails, cost controls, and deployment.

​Join TrueFoundry and HackerSquad for a full-day Agent Harness hackathon focused on building production-minded agentic applications. The goal is simple: take an agent use case from idea or prototype toward something that can be observed, governed, evaluated, and operated.

​TrueFoundry's AI Gateway, Agent Gateway, and MCP Gateway will frame the day. Builders will work on practical agent harness patterns such as model routing, controlled tool access, MCP workflows, observability, eval loops, fallback behavior, budget controls, governance, and deployment paths.

​This is a technical builder event, not a passive product pitch. Bring a laptop, a strong use case, and a willingness to build under realistic production constraints.

​What You Can Build

​An agent workflow with model routing, retries, and fallback behavior

​A tool-using agent with controlled MCP or API access

​An observability layer for traces, tool calls, latency, usage, cost, and failures

​An eval or test harness for agent behavior across repeated runs

​A governance pattern for permissions, approvals, logging, blocking, or escalation

​A deployment-minded agent application that shows how it would run inside a real team or platform environment

​Why This Gets Hard in Production

​Agent systems need to coordinate models, tools, permissions, memory, context, retries, and fallbacks without becoming brittle one-off glue code.

​Teams need traces, audit logs, usage visibility, cost attribution, and eval loops so they can understand what an agent did, why it did it, and what changed between runs.

​Scaling agents means managing quotas, budgets, latency, provider failures, tool access, and security policies across teams.

​Guardrails need to become runtime controls: clear rules for what data an agent can see, which tools it can call, which actions require human approval, and how unsafe requests or outputs get blocked, logged, or escalated.

​Deployment gets harder when agents need to connect to internal systems, respect governance rules, and stay reliable as usage grows.

​Who Should Apply

​Platform, infrastructure, and backend engineers building or operating AI agent systems

​AI engineers and product engineers working with LLMs, tool calling, MCP, evals, or agent workflows

​Technical founders moving agent prototypes toward production

​Security, DevOps, and ML platform practitioners thinking about governance, observability, and cost control

​Builders with a concrete agent use case and enough technical depth to build during the day

​Format

​Doors, check-in, coffee, and setup

​Welcome from HackerSquad / The Builder Collective and TrueFoundry

​TrueFoundry Agent Harness framing

​Challenge brief, build tracks, and judging rubric

​Focused build sprint with technical support available

​Project submissions and proof packages

​Selected demos, judging, awards, and closing remarks

​Follow-up conversations and networking

​Bring

​A laptop

​A concrete agent use case, workflow, prototype, or infrastructure problem

​Questions about model gateways, MCP tools, observability, evals, cost controls, deployment, or agent governance

​Any teammates you plan to build with

​Admission is free and approval-based because space is limited and the event is designed for technical builders working on relevant agent infrastructure and application problems. The exact South Bay venue and arrival details will be shared with approved attendees once the venue path is confirmed.

​When: Saturday, September 19, 2026 | 9:30 AM - 8:00 PM PT

​Where: 3120 Scott Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95054

About Event

​"The way to get startup ideas is not to try to think of startup ideas. It's to look for problems, preferably problems you have yourself." Paul Graham

​Most people who want to build something sit in a room and brainstorm ideas. That is the wrong starting point.

​The right starting point is a real problem. That is the ITCH worth scratching.

​If you do not have that problem yourself, come find it here.

​ITCH is a panel discussion with business owners or industry experts in the SF community. We dig into what is actually hard in their business right now. Together, we find the ITCH.

​You leave with a list of real problems you can actually work on. And some of the panelists might let you pilot your solution with them directly.

You can find ways to leverage AI for these problems.

​ITCHATHON

​Two days later we run the ITCHATHON, a hackathon where we solve the problems we found here. Sign up for that too →

​This is for anyone who wants to build something. A startup, a side project, or just something for your CV. Up to you.

​Come and leave with an ITCH.
September 24th, 6 PM

​Partners

Providing the physical and virtual infrastructure for European startups and investors to thrive in the U.S.

​
If you know a small or medium business owner who'd be great to invite to the panels, connect with me on LinkedIn.
